description: Scenarios evaluating individual Hindi phrases based on pragmatic usage, formality, and social context.

questions.scenario: You are arriving at a corporate office meeting in the morning and greeting your manager formally.
options: A casual greeting used only between close teenage friends at night.
A formal and respectful morning greeting suitable for professional or general use.
An apology for showing up late to a meeting.
A way of saying goodbye at the end of the workday.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Namaste' combined with 'suprabhatam' sets a polite, professional morning tone.

questions.scenario: You accidentally arrived twenty minutes late to an important client discussion.
questions.hindi: माफ़ कीजिए, मुझे देर हो गई है।
questions.roman: Maaf kijiye, mujhe der ho gayi hai.
options: Expressing excitement about meeting the client.
Asking for the price of a file or document.
Apologizing formally for being late.
Stating that everything is completely fine.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Maaf kijiye' (Excuse me/Sorry) paired with 'der ho gayi hai' is the standard professional apology.

questions.scenario: A colleague explains a complex project guideline, and you want to confirm you completely grasped it.
options: I don't know anything about this.
Can you repeat this instruction?
Yes, I have understood it.
Where is the meeting room?
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Samajh gaya hoon' confirms that you have processed and understood the information.

questions.scenario: Your peer asks if an urgent report is finalized and ready to submit.
options: This is absolutely correct and confirmed.
Maybe it will rain tomorrow.
Who is handling this task?
I am from Mumbai.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Bilkul sahi hai' validates that data or work is completely correct.

questions.scenario: You are making a polite request to a senior colleague who is speaking too quickly during a presentation.
options: Asking them to speak faster so you can leave.
Politely asking them to speak a little slower for clarity.
Telling them to stop talking immediately.
Complimenting their presentation style.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kripya' (Please) with 'thoda dheere boliye' (speak a little slowly) is a polite request for pace reduction.

questions.scenario: A coworker apologizes to you for a minor mistake on a draft document.
questions.hindi: कोई बात नहीं, चिंता मत कीजिए।
questions.roman: Koi baat nahin, chinta mat kijiye.
options: Expressing anger over the mistake.
Reassuring them politely that it's no problem and not to worry.
Asking them to redo the entire project by tonight.
Telling them that you don't know how to fix it.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Koi baat nahin' (No problem) + 'chinta mat kijiye' (don't worry) is an empathetic reassurance.

questions.scenario: You are introduced to a new team member at work for the first time.
options: Asking what time the meeting finishes.
Expressing polite pleasure upon meeting someone new.
Telling them that you are leaving the office.
Asking for their personal phone number.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Aapse milkar bahut khushi hui' translates directly to 'Very pleased to meet you'.

questions.scenario: You are asking a coworker about the scheduled timing of an upcoming team sync.
options: Asking for the location of the meeting room.
Inquiring about the scheduled time of the meeting.
Asking who will be attending the meeting.
Canceling the meeting altogether.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kab' means 'When', making this an inquiry about time.

questions.scenario: You are leaving the office for the day and saying goodbye to your teammates.
options: Greeting them good morning.
Saying goodbye and looking forward to seeing them tomorrow.
Asking them to join you for lunch right now.
Apologizing for leaving work early.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Alvida' (Goodbye) + 'kal phir milenge' (see you again tomorrow) is the standard end-of-day sign-off.

questions.scenario: A manager asks if you can take responsibility for an urgent client task.
questions.meaning: Sure, I am doing it right now.
options: Refusing the task due to lack of time.
Confidently accepting the task and committing to do it immediately.
Asking someone else to take over the work.
Stating that you don't understand the task.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Zaroor' (Sure) combined with 'main abhi karta hoon' shows prompt willingness to assist.

questions.scenario: You walk into a local store and want to ask the price of a fruit box.
options: Asking for directions to the nearest hospital.
Inquiring about the price of an item.
Complaining about bad quality produce.
Asking the store owner for their name.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kitni hai' combined with 'keemat' is used to ask for the price or cost of an item.

questions.scenario: You are boarding an office cab and want to tell the driver your destination city area.
questions.meaning: I want to go to Connaught Place.
options: Telling the driver you want to get down immediately.
Stating your intended destination location to the driver.
Asking the driver how much money they make.
Complaining about heavy traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Mujhe [Location] jana hai' is the standard way to declare your destination to transport drivers.

questions.scenario: A friend asks if you want to grab a cup of coffee together after office hours.
options: Politely rejecting the invitation to stay home.
Enthusiastically accepting an invitation to go somewhere.
Asking where the coffee shop is located.
Saying that you hate drinking coffee.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Haan, zaroor' shows strong agreement and enthusiasm for a plan or invitation.

questions.scenario: You are standing at a busy intersection and trying to find the nearest metro station.
questions.hindi: पास में मेट्रो स्टेशन कहाँ है?
questions.roman: Paas mein metro station kahan hai?
questions.meaning: Where is the nearby metro station?
options: Asking for the time of the next train.
Inquiring about the location of the nearest metro station.
Complaining about closed station gates.
Buying a token ticket from an attendant.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kahan hai' asks for location, and 'paas mein' specifies proximity ('nearby').

questions.scenario: You receive help from a stranger who helps you pick up your dropped documents.
options: Expressing deep gratitude and thanks for someone's assistance.
Asking them to help you with more office work.
Apologizing for dropping your papers on the floor.
Saying goodbye before walking away.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Bahut-bahut dhanyawad' emphasizes a heartfelt and heavy expression of thanks.

questions.scenario: You are explaining to a foreign colleague that you can speak both English and Hindi.
questions.hindi: मैं अंग्रेजी और हिंदी दोनों बोल सकता हूँ।
questions.roman: Main Angrezi aur Hindi dono bol sakta hoon.
questions.meaning: I can speak both English and Hindi.
options: Saying you can only read books in English.
Stating your capability to speak both English and Hindi languages.
Asking someone else to translate your conversation.
Expressing difficulty in learning new languages.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Dono bol sakta hoon' explicitly states bilingual speaking capability.

questions.scenario: You want to check if a specific restaurant table or seat is vacant for use.
options: Asking if a seat or table is unoccupied before sitting down.
Complaining that the chair is broken.
Ordering food from the restaurant waiter.
Asking for the restaurant bill.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Khaali hai' means 'is it empty/vacant', which is polite to ask before occupying a space.

questions.scenario: You want to order one cup of hot tea at a roadside tea stall.
questions.meaning: Brother, please give one cup of tea.
options: Ordering cold water from a vendor.
Placing an order for one cup of tea with a vendor.
Asking how much a cup of tea costs.
Complaining that the tea is too hot.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Ek cup chai dena' is the direct, standard way to place an order at a beverage stall.

questions.scenario: You are letting your teammate know that you are stepping out for a brief lunch break.
questions.hindi: मैं थोड़ी देर में वापस आता हूँ।
questions.roman: Main thodi der mein wapas aata hoon.
questions.meaning: I will be back in a little while.
options: Stating that you are leaving the office for the rest of the day.
Informing someone that you will return shortly after a brief absence.
Asking when your coworker is going out for lunch.
Telling them you forgot your laptop at home.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Thodi der mein wapas aata hoon' indicates a temporary absence with a quick return.

questions.scenario: You want to ask a shopkeeper if they accept digital UPI payments.
questions.hindi: क्या आप ऑनलाइन पेमेंट लेते हैं?
questions.roman: Kya aap online payment lete hain?
options: Asking if they only accept cash money.
Inquiring if digital online payments or UPI are accepted by the vendor.
Asking for a discount on your purchase total.
Complaining that your internet network is down.
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Online payment lete hain' checks whether digital transactions are supported at the store.

questions.scenario: You want to politely ask a stranger if they know the correct time.
questions.hindi: माफ़ कीजिए, क्या समय हुआ है?
questions.roman: Maaf kijiye, kya samay hua hai?
questions.meaning: Excuse me, what time is it?
options: Asking someone for the current time politely[cite: 12].
Asking for directions to the railway station[cite: 12].
Apologizing for arriving late to an appointment[cite: 12].
Inquiring about store operating hours[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Maaf kijiye' (Excuse me) combined with 'kya samay hua hai' is the polite way to ask for the time[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You are sitting in a meeting room and want to ask if the window can be opened for fresh air.
questions.hindi: क्या मैं खिड़की खोल सकता हूँ?
questions.roman: Kya main khidki khol sakta hoon?
options: Asking for permission to close the office door[cite: 12].
Asking for permission to open the window[cite: 12].
Complaining about cold air coming inside[cite: 12].
Asking someone to clean the glass panes[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kya main... khol sakta hoon' is the standard way to request permission to open something like a window[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to tell someone that you do not understand a particular point they made.
questions.hindi: मुझे यह बात समझ में नहीं आई।
questions.roman: Mujhe yeh baat samajh mein nahi aai.
questions.meaning: I did not understand this point.
options: Stating clearly that you have fully understood the instruction[cite: 12].
Expressing that a specific point or statement is not clear to you[cite: 12].
Asking the speaker to repeat their full name[cite: 12].
Refusing to participate in the conversation[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Samajh mein nahi aai' politely indicates confusion or lack of clarity regarding a topic[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask a colleague to say a phrase again because you missed it.
questions.hindi: क्या आप इसे दोहरा सकते हैं?
questions.roman: Kya aap ise dohra sakte hain?
options: Asking someone to write down an email address[cite: 12].
Politely requesting someone to repeat what they just said[cite: 12].
Telling someone to stop speaking immediately[cite: 12].
Asking for a translation of a document[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Dohra sakte hain' translates directly to 'can you repeat/iterate this'[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You are wishing your friend a speedy recovery after hearing they caught a fever.
options: Congratulating someone on their promotion[cite: 12].
Wishing someone a speedy recovery from an illness[cite: 12].
Telling someone to hurry up for a meeting[cite: 12].
Saying goodbye before going to sleep[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Jaldi se theek ho jao' is the standard warm wish for someone who is sick[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask someone where they live or which city they are from.
options: Inquiring about someone's residential city or location[cite: 12].
Asking for directions to a restaurant[cite: 12].
Asking someone where they left their car keys[cite: 12].
Inquiring about office seating arrangements[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kahan rehte hain' asks directly about where a person resides[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to express that you are feeling very happy today.
options: Stating that you are feeling tired and sleepy[cite: 12].
Expressing a joyful and happy mood for the day[cite: 12].
Complaining about bad weather conditions[cite: 12].
Expressing frustration over delayed work[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Bahut khush hoon' clearly communicates a state of happiness[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask a friend about their family members and how everyone is doing.
options: Asking about the well-being of family members at home[cite: 12].
Inquiring about household grocery expenses[cite: 12].
Asking if anyone is home right now[cite: 12].
Asking for directions to a family member's office[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Ghar par sab kaise hain' is a customary polite inquiry about family health and well-being[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to let someone know that you will call them later in the evening.
questions.hindi: मैं आपको बाद में कॉल करता हूँ।
questions.roman: Main aapko baad mein call karta hoon.
options: Telling someone you are calling them right now[cite: 12].
Informing someone that you will initiate a phone call later[cite: 12].
Asking someone to delete your phone number[cite: 12].
Complaining about poor mobile phone network signals[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Baad mein call karta hoon' communicates an intention to connect at a later time[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask a shopkeeper if they have a specific item in stock.
options: Asking if a particular item or product is available in the store[cite: 12].
Asking for a refund on a broken product[cite: 12].
Inquiring about store opening timings[cite: 12].
Asking the price of a delivered parcel[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Saaman mil jayega' checks product availability at a shop[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask someone if they need any help with their heavy bags.
questions.hindi: क्या मैं आपकी मदद कर सकता हूँ?
questions.roman: Kya main aapki madad kar sakta hoon?
options: Asking someone if they require assistance or help[cite: 12].
Asking someone to help you carry your own luggage[cite: 12].
Refusing help offered by a colleague[cite: 12].
Asking for directions to the help desk[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Madad kar sakta hoon' is the standard polite offer to assist someone[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to express that you are extremely busy with work today.
options: Stating that you have a completely free day[cite: 12].
Informing someone that you are currently very busy with tasks[cite: 12].
Asking someone to keep you busy with work[cite: 12].
Complaining about boredom at the office[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Bahut vyast hoon' means 'I am very busy'[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask a friend what plans they have for the upcoming weekend.
questions.meaning: What is the plan for this weekend?
options: Asking about someone's schedule or plans for the weekend[cite: 12].
Talking about what happened last weekend[cite: 12].
Asking for office holiday notifications[cite: 12].
Canceling a weekend movie trip[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Kya plan hai' combined with 'weekend' inquires about upcoming leisure activities[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to suggest to your friend that you should meet soon.
options: Suggesting that you and someone should catch up or meet soon[cite: 12].
Stating that you never want to see someone again[cite: 12].
Asking someone why they are avoiding you[cite: 12].
Saying goodbye at the airport terminal[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Jald hi milna chahiye' expresses a desire to meet up in the near future[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to tell someone to take care of themselves as you part ways.
options: Telling someone to take good care of themselves[cite: 12].
Asking someone to look after your belongings[cite: 12].
Reminding someone to pay their medical bills[cite: 12].
Complaining about poor health conditions[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Apna khyal rakhna' is a warm parting phrase meaning 'take care'[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask someone if they like drinking tea or coffee.
questions.hindi: आपको चाय पसंद है या कॉफ़ी?
questions.roman: Aapko chai pasand hai ya coffee?
questions.meaning: Do you like tea or coffee?
options: Asking someone to choose between tea or coffee preferences[cite: 12].
Telling someone that you hate both tea and coffee[cite: 12].
Ordering beverages for a business meeting[cite: 12].
Asking how to brew coffee beans[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Pasand hai ya coffee' asks about beverage preferences[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to tell someone that you don't know the answer to their question.
questions.hindi: मुझे इसके बारे में नहीं पता।
questions.roman: Mujhe iske bare mein nahi pata.
options: Stating clearly that you have no information or knowledge about a topic[cite: 12].
Explaining a complex topic in detail[cite: 12].
Asking someone to teach you something new[cite: 12].
Denying involvement in a mistake[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Nahi pata' indicates a lack of awareness or knowledge about a matter[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to wish someone good luck before they go into an interview.
options: Offering best wishes and good luck for an upcoming endeavor[cite: 12].
Congratulating someone after winning a lottery[cite: 12].
Saying happy birthday to a colleague[cite: 12].
Expressing condolences for a loss[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Shubhkaamnaayein' translates directly to good wishes[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to ask someone how their day at work went.
options: Inquiring how someone's day went or progressed[cite: 12].
Asking what time the workday ends[cite: 12].
Complaining about a long working day[cite: 12].
Asking about tomorrow's office schedule[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Din kaisa raha' is a friendly way to ask about someone's daily experience[cite: 12].

questions.scenario: You want to tell someone that you completely agree with their opinion.
options: Expressing full agreement with someone's point or opinion[cite: 12].
Stating a strong disagreement during a debate[cite: 12].
Asking someone to change their mind[cite: 12].
Telling someone that you don't understand their view[cite: 12].
questions.explanation: Correct! 'Sehmat hoon' means 'I am in agreement with you'[cite: 12].
